name: LOTUS
title: Semantic Operators: A Declarative Model for Rich, AI-based Data Processing
summary: Natural-language specifications for filtering, joining, sorting and aggregation, with optimized implementations evaluated against a reference algorithm.
caveat: Accuracy guarantees are relative to a chosen gold algorithm; they are not guarantees of factual correctness.

name: UQE
title: UQE: A Query Engine for Unstructured Databases
summary: A SQL-like language for reasoning over images, conversations and reviews, combining foundation models with sampling and execution optimization.
caveat: Published evaluation covers selected query types and datasets; capabilities should not be generalized to arbitrary analytics.

name: Palimpzest
title: A Declarative System for Optimizing AI Workloads
summary: Turns declarative AI analytics into executable plans that trade off output quality, runtime and model cost.
caveat: This record describes the 2024 prototype; it is not a specification of every capability in the current project.

name: DocETL
title: DocETL: Agentic Query Rewriting and Evaluation for Complex Document Processing
summary: Rewrites complex document workflows by decomposing tasks and data, using agents to propose and evaluate better execution plans.
caveat: Agent-generated validation and reported accuracy gains depend on the task and evaluation design.

name: SUQL
title: SUQL: Conversational Search over Structured and Unstructured Data with Large Language Models
summary: Composes structured queries with free-text answering and summarization, supporting conversational access to hybrid knowledge sources.
caveat: The paper studies hybrid access and semantic parsing; it is not a broad benchmark of semantic engine optimization.

name: SemBench
title: SemBench: A Benchmark for Semantic Query Processing Engines
summary: Evaluates semantic engines across text, image and audio scenarios using filters, joins, mappings, ranking and classification.
caveat: Results are a snapshot of evolving systems, models and configurations; they do not establish a permanent leaderboard.

name: LROBench
title: Large Language Model-Enhanced Relational Operators: Taxonomy, Benchmark, and Analysis
summary: Organizes Select, Match, Impute, Cluster and Order operators into single-operator and multi-operator workloads over relational databases.
caveat: Operator-level findings depend on model, implementation and workload; the benchmark complements rather than replaces end-to-end evaluation.

name: Sema
title: Sema: A High-performance System for LLM-based Semantic Query Processing
summary: Integrates semantic expressions into SQL and combines logical rewrites with adaptive reordering, fusion and prompt batching.
caveat: Preprint results cover 20 queries and selected baselines; no independent reproduction is claimed here.

name: NousDB
title: NousDB - A Fast Query Engine for Semantic Analytics
summary: A DataFusion-based engine using semantic algebra, token histograms and context-aware batching to optimize AI analytics.
caveat: October 2026 preprint. Batching guarantees have specific statistical assumptions; reported speedups are workload-specific.

name: JEVDB
title: Prune First, Decide Fast: Scalable Semantic Query Processing with JEVDB
summary: Uses decision models for semantic operations, escalates uncertain cases to generative models and prunes semantic-join candidates.
caveat: October 2026 preprint. Necessary-condition screening and evaluated decision models determine the scope of pruning claims.

name: SemViews
title: Semantic Views: Certified Reuse of LLM Labels Across Semantic Queries
summary: Reuses prior query labels as ranking signals and applies fresh stratified oracle sampling to certify filter precision and recall.
caveat: October 2026 preprint. Guarantees concern agreement with an oracle under the stated sampling assumptions, not human truth.

name: Same Query, Different Answer
title: Same Query, Different Answer: Run-to-Run Variance in Semantic Query Processing
summary: Studies how repeated model decisions propagate into changing query answers and proposes reporting practices for reproducible evaluation.
caveat: October 2026 preprint. This is an evaluation study rather than a new engine; findings concern the tested models and workloads.

name: SemBaker
title: From Interpretation to Compilation: A Compilation-Based Execution Engine for Semantic Operator Systems
summary: Compiles suitable semantic operations into local Python functions, routing between compiled and native execution using cost estimates.
caveat: Compilation applies to selected operators; generated code is not a universal substitute for semantic model inference.

name: Kalypso
title: Kalypso: Relational LLM Serving
summary: Makes model serving aware of semantic operator dependencies, pipelining tuples to reuse KV-cache state under memory constraints.
caveat: A serving substrate rather than a complete user-facing query engine; benefits depend on cache reuse and workload structure.

name: FlockMTL
title: Beyond Quacking: Deep Integration of Language Models and RAG into DuckDB
summary: Adds model-backed scalar and aggregate functions, with PROMPT and MODEL schema objects plus batching and caching optimizations.
caveat: The cited publication is a short system paper; consult project documentation for deployment and supported models.

name: iPDB
title: iPDB -- Optimizing Semantic SQL Queries
summary: Supports in-database ML and LLM inference through a relational predict operator and optimizations across semantic SQL operations.
caveat: The current paper title differs from earlier citations. Performance comparisons apply to the evaluated configurations.

name: PLOP
title: PLOP: Cost-Based Placement of Semantic Operators in Hybrid Query Plans
summary: Balances model-call cost against relational processing cost when choosing semantic operator placement in mixed query plans.
caveat: The current record is titled PLOP, not Horrila. Rewrites and cost analysis rely on the paper's stated semantics and caching assumptions.

name: Relational LLM optimization
title: Optimizing LLM Queries in Relational Data Analytics Workloads
summary: Reorders table rows and fields to increase shared prompt prefixes and improve KV-cache reuse during batch model inference.
caveat: Reported cost savings depend on model-serving behavior and provider pricing; this catalog does not repeat them as current estimates.

name: LLM ORDER BY
title: Access Paths for Efficient Ordering with Large Language Models
summary: Studies physical implementations of semantic ordering and a budget-aware optimizer that chooses among ranking access paths.
caveat: No single sorting implementation dominates all evaluated datasets; quality assessment includes model-based judging.

name: Larch
title: Larch: Learned Query Optimization for Semantic Predicates
summary: Learns per-row evaluation orders for semantic predicates, using either a sequential decision policy or predicted selectivities.
caveat: The reported reductions concern tested workloads and baselines; training and runtime overhead should be considered in new deployments.

name: Fast semantic filtering
title: Fast LLM-Based Semantic Filtering: From a Unified Framework to an Adaptive Two-Phase Method
summary: Combines clustering and learned proxies adaptively, using token-aware representations and oracle confidence to reduce expensive filtering calls.
caveat: Empirical attainment of an accuracy target is not an unconditional guarantee; the oracle itself may be wrong.

name: SemJoin
title: SemJoin: Semantic Join Optimization
summary: Uses an LLM advisor to route joins between clustering-based candidate pruning and classification into a shared label space.
caveat: Short preprint evaluated on three datasets; routing success on those workloads does not establish universal optimality.

name: UDA-Bench
title: Unstructured Data Analysis using LLMs: A Comprehensive Benchmark
summary: Evaluates unstructured-document analysis against manually annotated relational views. The arXiv v1 workload contains five datasets and 240 queries covering extraction, filtering, aggregation, joins, and combinations of operators.
caveat: Ground truth is defined over selected schema attributes, so coverage does not extend to arbitrary open-ended document questions. Dataset counts differ between the cited arXiv version and repository descriptions; specify the artifact version when reporting results.
reviewNote: Publication record and benchmark-construction sections reviewed. The workload evaluates accuracy, model cost, and latency. No experiments were rerun.

name: Shelob
title: Prune First, Decide Fast: Scalable Semantic Query Processing with JEVDB
summary: Extends TPC-DS-derived relations with return reports, issue bulletins, and release notes to study semantic-join scaling. The JEVDB paper evaluates five queries at XS, S, and M tiers.
caveat: Introduced and evaluated by the JEVDB authors. The full SF1 workload is larger than the measured tiers; its candidate count must not be presented as an executed comparison. Shelob is not an official TPC benchmark or an independent validation of JEVDB.
reviewNote: Reviewed the experimental setup and Shelob evaluation sections of the JEVDB paper. The protocol reports answer F1, cost, latency, and timeout progress. No experiments were rerun.

resources.label: Shelob evaluation in the JEVDB paper

name: Spider 2.0-AIFunc
title: Spider 2.0-AIFunc: Extending Real-World Text-to-SQL to AI-Native SQL Workflows
interface: Natural language to SQL with AI functions
summary: Tests whether models generate Snowflake SQL that composes relational operations with AI functions for classification, filtering, sentiment analysis, extraction, similarity, and aggregation.
caveat: Evaluates SQL generation, not engine execution performance. The paper reports 465 instances; the public task release contains 393. Gold SQL and database resources are not bundled, and official scoring requires additional access.

name: VectorSQLBench
title: Text2VectorSQL: Towards a Unified Interface for Vector Search and SQL Queries
interface: Natural language to SQL with vector search
summary: Benchmarks generation of queries combining relational operations and vector search, spanning three database backends and four source collections. Examines result omissions when SQL filters interact with vector retrieval.
caveat: An adjacent query-generation benchmark. Vector similarity is a retrieval operation and does not establish the quality or efficiency of arbitrary model-backed filters, joins, or aggregations.

name: HybridDeepResearch
title: Benchmarking Hybrid Deep Research Across Database Querying and Web Search
interface: Agents combining SQL and web search
summary: Evaluates agents on 380 tasks requiring both database queries and web evidence. Tasks exercise database-to-search, search-to-database, and parallel reasoning, with an emphasis on preserving constraints across tools.
caveat: Measures agent coordination and final-answer correctness across tools. It does not isolate semantic operator execution or query optimizer performance, and web evidence can change over time.

name: The Stochastic Shift
title: The Stochastic Shift: A New Evaluation Paradigm for Text-to-SQL with AI Operators
interface: Evaluation of SQL containing AI operators
summary: Studies failures of exact-result scoring for SQL with stochastic AI operators. Proposes evaluating relational logic and semantic operations separately, with experiments on BigQuery and ThalamusDB.
caveat: An evaluation framework rather than a general-purpose workload benchmark. Reported validation accuracy applies to the tested query sets and judging protocol, not all SQL translations or semantic predicates.
